info.name: AI Support Ticket Triage Agent - Current API
info.description: Postman requests for the HTTP functionality wired in the current development branch: health, Keycloak-authenticated identity/tenant and ticket APIs, document evidence, ticket workflows, tenant-configured SLA and reports, plus Jira webhook intake. Set the blank variables before running. For login, use Postman OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code (With PKCE): Auth URL http://{{keycloakHost}}:{{keycloakPort}}/realms/{{realm}}/protocol/openid-connect/auth; Access Token URL http://{{keycloakHost}}:{{keycloakPort}}/realms/{{realm}}/protocol/openid-connect/token; Client ID support-web; scope openid; S256; no client secret. Add Postman's callback URI to the support-web client's valid redirect URIs in Keycloak. After Postman receives a token, copy it into accessToken and the relevant role variable(s); use separate tokens for distinct users/roles. The API also requires an active local user and membership; X-Organisation-ID selects a tenant but does not grant access. Jira ingestion uses the configured secret in the URL, not a bearer token. For Jira, configure JIRA_TENANT_CONFIG in backend/.env. This is a local-development test collection: do not export real tokens or secrets. AI analysis components, generic extracted-rule review, and generic policy routes are not exposed as HTTP routes in the current backend and are intentionally not included.

item.name: List my organisations
item.description: Use the returned organisation id as organisationId. If the list is empty, the user needs an active application membership.

item.name: Create organisation
item.description: The caller needs organisations.create and a valid selected tenant context.

item.name: Invite user
item.description: User invitation requires the Keycloak admin service client to be configured in backend/.env.

item.name: Change ticket status
item.description: Use a transition allowed by the active workflow; the default example is OPEN.

item.name: Upload ticket attachment
item.description: Select a file for the file form-data field in Postman.

item.name: Upload document
item.description: Select a UTF-8 .txt file in Postman.

exec: if (pm.response.code === 201) { const result = pm.response.json(); pm.collectionVariables.set('documentId', result.data.document.id); pm.collectionVariables.set('documentVersionId', result.data.version.id); }

item.name: Create tenant SLA policy
item.description: The numeric targets are illustrative test values only. Replace them with targets approved by the tenant. A successful 201 response saves slaPolicyId and slaVersionId.

exec: if (pm.response.code === 201) { const result = pm.response.json(); pm.collectionVariables.set('slaPolicyId', result.data.policy.id); pm.collectionVariables.set('slaVersionId', result.data.version.id); }

item.name: Run tenant SLA evaluations
item.description: Only tickets with an internal priority matching an active policy target are evaluated. Jira source priority is retained as source metadata and is not automatically translated.

item.name: Ingest Jira issue created or updated
item.description: Set jiraWebhookSecret and jiraReporterAccountId to match backend JIRA_TENANT_CONFIG. Jira reporter accountId must have an internal user mapping. The first call should return 201; a repeated event is idempotent.
